title: San Joaquin Valley Agricultural Phenology
headline: Seasonal crop phenology reveals harvest dynamics across 245 km² of irrigated agricultural fields.
story: California's Central Valley is one of the world's most productive agricultural regions. Throughout spring and summer, fields of almonds, alfalfa, tomatoes, and cotton undergo rapid phenological shifts. NISAR L-band polarimetry (HH/HV) probes the crop canopy volume, soil roughness, and moisture content with surgical precision, revealing field-by-field harvest and planting rhythms without needing cloud-free skies.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: Morning tule fog frequently obscures optical imagery in California's Central Valley; SAR satellites monitor crop growth status through fog cycles and during night orbits.

story_steps.title: Spring Pre-Planting Baseline
story_steps.description: Smooth bare soil fields scatter microwave energy specularly, creating distinct low backscatter signatures.

story_steps.title: Midsummer Canopy Development
story_steps.description: Dense crop biomass produces strong volume scattering, brightening individual rectangular parcels in radar images.

story_steps.title: Field-by-Field Biomass Change
story_steps.description: Change detection polygons clearly delineate individual irrigated parcel boundaries and harvest progressions.

story_steps.title: Soil Moisture & Water Optimization
story_steps.description: L-band dielectric sensitivity empowers water managers to verify irrigation timing and drought fallowing policies.
